about: Cantina Terlano, or Kellerei Terlan in German, was founded in 1893 by 24 growers in the village of Terlano, between Bolzano and Merano in South Tyrol. Today more than 150 member families farm about 190 hectares of steep vineyards from 250 to 900 metres up the slopes of the Tschöggelberg. The cooperative is famous for something unusual in Italy: white wines built to age for decades, and Pinot Bianco is its flagship grape, often compared to white Burgundy for its elegance and restraint.

Terlano’s vineyards sit on volcanic quartz porphyry, a reddish bedrock topped with sandy, quartz-rich soils that limit the vines’ vigour, keep berries small and give the wines their recognisable mineral, saline edge. For the Tradition Pinot Bianco, the estate-style entry wine, grapes are hand-picked and selected, gently pressed, settled naturally and slowly fermented at cool temperatures in stainless steel. The wine then rests on its fine lees in steel tanks for six to seven months, which adds texture without any oak flavour.

The cellar describes crisp apple and pear with hints of raspberry, lime, chamomile and lemongrass, then pear and quince on a balanced, lively palate with salty minerality. Falstaff’s tasters found crunchy apple, pear, apricot, white flowers and a touch of saltstone in the 2023, with finely integrated acidity and a slight creaminess. It is a fresh, food-friendly white, and a good introduction to a house whose top Pinot Bianco bottlings can age for decades.
facts: 6–7 months on the lees in steel tanks
